name: Question 2
worked_solution:
Let $u=1-x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=1-u.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\sqrt{1-x}\,\text{d}x & =-\int (1-u)^{2}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int ({u}^{2}-2u+1)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int ({u}^{5/2}-2{u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-(\frac{2}{7}{u}^{7/2}-\frac{4}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{7}\sqrt{(1-x)^{7}}+\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{(1-x)^{5}}-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{(1-x)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Let u=1−x. Then, we have dudx=−1⟹dx=−du.

We also note that x=1−u.

Now we can solve the integral in terms of u, and then express our final answer in terms of x:

∫x21−xdx=−∫(1−u)2udu=−∫(u2−2u+1)udu=−∫(u5/2−2u3/2+u1/2)du=−(27u7/2−45u5/2+23u3/2)+C=−27(1−x)7+45(1−x)5−23(1−x)3+C
